findings.title: The system assigns the customer number
findings.legacy: The Add path clears the customer number, calls the add program, and shows the number the program returns. The clerk never types it.
findings.firstPass: Required the clerk to type a customer number and stored whatever was entered.
findings.repair: Customer Add locks the number field and the application assigns the next identifier inside one database transaction.

findings.title: Customer update retrieves before it edits
findings.legacy: Update first inquires the live record, puts it on the screen, receives the clerk's edits, and only then writes the change.
findings.firstPass: Sent the update straight away from whatever happened to be in the form.
findings.repair: Update is now two steps: retrieve the record by customer number, then edit and save the loaded values.

regressionChecks.name: customer update loads before editable fields open

findings.title: Motor inquiry needs customer and policy number
findings.legacy: The inquiry passes both numbers and the query filters on both, so a policy is only shown to the customer who holds it.
findings.firstPass: Looked a policy up by policy number alone and disabled the customer-number field.
findings.repair: Inquiry requires both identifiers and returns not found when they do not belong together.

findings.title: The database assigns the policy number
findings.legacy: Add never copies a clerk-entered policy number. The insert lets the database allocate one and returns it.
findings.firstPass: Required the clerk to type a policy number and stored it as given.
findings.repair: Motor Add locks the policy-number field and the application assigns the identifier.

findings.title: Delete is keyed by customer and policy
findings.legacy: Delete passes both numbers and the DELETE statement matches on both, so one customer cannot remove another customer's policy.
findings.firstPass: Deleted by policy number alone, with the customer-number field disabled.
findings.repair: Delete requires both identifiers; a mismatched pair deletes nothing and returns not found.

findings.title: Motor update retrieves first, keyed by both numbers
findings.legacy: Update inquires with both numbers, shows the record, takes the clerk's edits, then updates through a cursor that filters on customer and policy.
findings.firstPass: Sent the update directly and targeted the row by policy number alone.
findings.repair: Update retrieves with both identifiers first, keeps the policy number locked, and writes only where both match.

regressionChecks.name: motor update loads with both identifiers before editing

uncertain.title: Exact identifier sequence
uncertain.detail: Customer numbers come from a CICS named counter and policy numbers from the database. The exact next value cannot be reproduced without running the mainframe, so Heirloom claims only that the system assigns the number.

uncertain.title: Deleting a policy that does not exist
uncertain.detail: The source comment says a missing record counts as success, but the SQLCODE check that follows treats it as an error. Heirloom records this as cannot determine and does not claim a match.

uncertain.title: Two claim-menu options on SSMAPP5
uncertain.detail: The policy-claim screen defines Inquire and Add options, but no LGTESTP5 presentation program exists in the source tree. Both stay screen-only and cannot determine.

uncertain.title: Date format enforcement
uncertain.detail: The legacy screens show yyyy-mm-dd, but the source does not prove the format is validated. No date rule was invented.
